description:
User approved version 3 of /Users/j5n/Workspace/fz-nml-29-private-append.html, verbatim "agreed. this is a good place to start." (in JSON's session, relayed by JSON and Optimize, 2026-11-19). Rulings: steps 2 and 2b land first, ahead of fz-nml.28's measurement; step 3 waits for fz-nml.28; Optimize builds fz-nml.29; Binary Handling's fz-9e2.6 and fz-9e2.10 build on 2 and 2b. Step 2. Builder: Optimize.
The list link's alias bit (LIST_LINK_ALIAS_MASK, bit 60 on arm64 / 61 on x86-64) in word 0 of a small bitstring and of a BinView, behind one accessor. The length readers (bitstring_bit_len, emit_binary_bit_len) and the three readers of a view's BinRef word (BinView::binref, the collector's rewrite in gc/trace.rs, deep copy) mask it. Views are born clear or set by the birth table on the page (FilledBuffer, GrownBuffer, AppendedInPlace clear; WindowOfBuffer set and marks its source; StaticLiteral, MessageCopy set); a function that returns its argument marks it. Heap::share and publish_contained_parts handle BITSTRING and BINVIEW. Nothing reads the mark yet.
Step zero: a dump-based test that Share precedes the <> call when the left operand is retained, on the native tail, native delivered and interpreter paths.
Acceptance: a fixture per publish point (tuple field, struct field, list head, map key, map value, closure capture, call Share, self-send, reduction yield) asserting the published binary reads back unchanged and its mark is set, through the runtime accessor step 3 will read (no test-only hook); a copy into another process is set; a slice and its source are both set; the mark survives minor and major collection, including the collector's rewrite of a view's first word; every bitstring test, fixture and bit-match path unchanged; no heap statistic changes.

comments.text: Correction to match the approved page (fz-nml-29-private-append.html v3 §221): 'a copy into another process is set' applies to a view (born MessageCopy). A small bitstring copied into another process is a fresh private object and is born clear, so its receiver can append in place. Pin it that way. The ticket text came from Optimize's proposal and mis-transcribed the page; the page is what the user approved.

PR #789 (CI). Fixtures 01711 (count per publish point, 3 paths), 01712 (owner + published holder both append, each keeps its bytes); block 01700-01719 used through 01712. Native reduction yield DOES mark (continuation captures args via store_closure_capture_ref_word; page §225 right); interp keeps its frame and marks nothing; pinned per path in 01711. Step 3 impact: an accumulator loop copies once after each yield on native.

title: A binary has a shared mark that every publish point sets
